rationale: Internally consistent and a substantive (not cosmetic) change to the archive's best signal — but it is largely a re-deflated version of the published cash-based operating profitability measure (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev), and the NOA-style denominator can go negative for net-operating-liability firms, flipping the ratio's sign in a way 1% winsorization will not repair.

A legitimate and diagnostically informative ratio-vs-interaction decomposition whose sign logic checks out, though its cross-sectional ordering will be dominated by the NOA/assets z-score and thus risks largely reproducing the published net-operating-assets anomaly with a profitability tilt.

This is essentially a rank-transform plus industry-neutralization wrapper on the archived AccrualGradedProfitability, and the stated claim that it "holds the economic content fixed" is wrong — replacing a signed z-score multiplier with a non-negative rank eliminates the sign-flip mechanism, converting a conditional interaction into a conjunctive rank product.

Under the actual Compustat convention (RECCH/INVCH are decrease-positive cash-flow items), the expression assigns the *long* leg to profitable firms building receivables and inventory, which directly contradicts the stated hypothesis, and the sign flip is justified only by back-fitting to a single inverted t-stat from the archived sign-based version.

Sign logic is correct under APALCH's increase-positive convention and the asset-vs-liability-side asymmetry in accrual quality is a genuinely new channel, but AOLOCH is a noisy residual grab-bag and this is the fourth instance of the same RANK(oibdp/at)×NEG(IND_ZSCORE(·)) template in the batch.

Internally inconsistent: oibdp is measured *before* depreciation, so multiplying it by D&A intensity systematically favors firms whose EBITDA is high only because their true (post-depreciation) profitability is low, which is the opposite of the "equally profitable but conservative" firms the hypothesis describes — and within-industry D&A/assets is mostly an asset-age/capital-intensity proxy rather than a conservatism proxy.
